name: comp-122

frames.best_why: All four branded buttons are stacked neatly with no cursor covering any of them.

tagline: Four solid brand-coloured login buttons, one provider per row.
summary: A stack of four full-width buttons for signing in through Google, X, Facebook or GitHub, each filled with a saturated brand colour and led by a small brand glyph.
appearance: Four rounded full-width buttons stack with narrow gaps on a near-black stage: a red Google tile, a near-black X tile, a bright blue Facebook tile and a charcoal GitHub tile. A faint white brand mark sits at the left of each and the white label is roughly centred.
behaviour: Hovering a row darkens its fill slightly and nothing else moves; each button is otherwise a static sign-in target that would launch its provider's flow.
demo_content: The labels "Login with Google", "Login with X", "Login with Facebook" and "Login with GitHub".
search_phrases: sign in with google facebook github
use_when: A sign-in or sign-up screen offers several third-party providers as full-width one-click choices.
avoid_when: Colours are hardcoded, Google sits on a red tile, and none of the buttons has a click handler.
customise: No props are exposed: the four providers, their brand fills and their labels are literals, so adding or removing one means editing the file.
weight_why: Four static buttons with fixed brand fills and a simple hover dim.

a11y.note: Each label names its provider as real text and focus is ringed; the dimmed icons add nothing for screen readers.

issues: Google sits on a red tile with a faded G, unlike Google's own white sign-in button.
None of the buttons has a click handler, so they look like logins but do nothing.
polish_why: Evenly stacked buttons; brand accuracy is off and the icons look washed out.
